conventions.convention: Small extensions are surjections of finite-dimensional local Artin k-algebras with residue field k whose kernel is annihilated by the source maximal ideal. The kernel may be zero and need not be principal.

Deformations include a specified identification of the special fibre; their isomorphisms induce its identity. Relative lifts fix the entire intermediate deformation. Augmented bases include k[I] with arbitrary-dimensional I.

The ordinary scheme cotangent complex uses cohomological degrees ≤0 and a global sheaf-ring resolution. Cartesian base-change comparison is an isomorphism under Tor-independence, including flat base change.

Ext of complexes is global derived Hom, equivalently derived-category Hom into M[i]. Ordinary Hom of two-term complexes requires projective terms, or the separately stated global-section acyclicity condition.

Embedded deformations retain the fixed ambient scheme; an isomorphism is over that ambient scheme. Equation classification assumes n≥2, d≥1 and a smooth hypersurface of pure dimension n−1; residue-normalized equations are equivalent precisely by unit multiplication.

An abelian scheme has smooth proper locally finitely presented structure morphism and nonempty connected geometric fibres of the specified constant dimension g. Projectivity over a general base is not assumed.

A Néron model is smooth, separated and finite type, with the mapping property for every smooth test scheme. Uniqueness fixes the specified generic-fibre identification. Weak Néron models require only extension of étale local points.

An S-rational map has an actual representative on an open dense in every fibre. For separated targets representatives glue; domain formation is asserted to commute with flat base change, not arbitrary base change.

The Tate module is indexed by ν≥1 with multiplication-by-ℓ transition maps. Inertia is Gal(Ksep/Ksh); unramified means its pointwise trivial action. Arithmetic reduction results require ℓ different from the residue characteristic.

The relative Picard functor is an fppf sheaf on arbitrary test schemes. Degree zero means fibrewise algebraic triviality, not numerical degree in higher dimension; bundles are rigidified along the identity.
A polarization need only be realized by an ample line bundle after algebraic closure. Its degree is the finite locally free rank of the isogeny, retaining nonreduced kernel lengths.
Néron existence is asserted over arbitrary DVRs, without excellence, completeness, perfect residue field or reduction-type assumptions; AC and DC remain explicit.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and DC. Over a regular Noetherian base S, an S-rational map from a smooth S-scheme Z into a smooth separated finite-type S-group scheme G, defined at every height-one point of Z, extends uniquely to an S-morphism Z→G.

Assume AC and DC. For an abelian variety A over the fraction field of any DVR R, there is a smooth separated finite-type model V with V(Rsh)=A(Ksh). A weak model collection receives generic rational maps from smooth R-schemes with irreducible special fibre as R-rational maps into a member, and remains weak after localization at a special-fibre generic point.

Assume AC and DC. A separated flat finite-type scheme over an arbitrary DVR with smooth generic fibre admits a finite sequence of special-fibre blowups, proper and generically isomorphisms, whose smooth locus contains every Rsh-section.

Assume AC and DC. A smooth separated faithfully flat finite-type Rsh-scheme with a strict birational group law has a smooth separated finite-type group completion obtained by finitely many section translates, containing the original scheme as a fibre-dense open. Group completions are canonically unique, also after arbitrary base change under the stated finite-presentation hypotheses.

Assume AC and DC. For a projective geometrically integral k-scheme A, sufficiently positive effective divisors of fixed Hilbert polynomial form finite-type open Hilbert charts; the positive chart maps to the fppf Picard sheaf as a smooth projective-space bundle on arbitrary tests; the Picard diagonal is represented and quasi-compact, and a Picard representative is separated.

Assume AC and DC. For an abelian variety A of dimension g over an algebraically closed field, dim H¹(A,O_A)≤g and this cohomology is the Picard tangent space; Pic⁰ is smooth proper connected of dimension g; every ample line bundle gives a Mumford isogeny A→Pic⁰ with finite scheme-theoretic kernel.

Assume AC and DC. Over any field, the algebraically trivial rigidified Picard subfunctor of an abelian variety A is represented by an abelian variety A∨ of dimension dim A, with normalized Poincaré bundle and full universal property compatible with field extension.

Assume AC and DC. The Mumford homomorphism of a line bundle M on an abelian variety vanishes exactly for Pic⁰ classes; nontrivial homogeneous line bundles have zero cohomology in every degree. Over algebraic closure every homogeneous bundle is a translate difference of a fixed ample bundle; the kernel equality holds as a sheaf on all tests.

Assume AC and DC. For a separated étale finite-type scheme H over a strictly henselian local ring R with separably closed residue field k, reduction H(R)→H(k) is bijective. The section images form a finite étale disjoint union of copies of Spec R containing the whole closed fibre; the complement has no closed fibre or sections.
Assume AC and DC. A smooth separated finite-type quasi-projective scheme G over a DVR, with abelian generic fibre and proper geometrically connected special fibre, is proper over the DVR.

Assume AC. For a polynomial presentation R=A[x]→B with kernel I and a free relation presentation F→I with kernel Q, the Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger complex Q/F₀→F⊗_R B→Ω_R/A⊗_R B identifies with τ≥−2 L_B/A. Its ordinary Hom cohomology computes Extⁱ_B(L_B/A,M) for i=0,1,2, with the displayed T¹ and T² cokernels.

Assume AC. For a square-zero extension A′→A with kernel I, a flat A-algebra B, a B-module N and prescribed A-linear c:I→N, square-zero A′-algebra extensions B′→B with identified kernel N have canonical obstruction in Ext²_B(L_B/A,N), vanishing exactly when solutions exist; solution classes then form an Ext¹-torsor and automorphisms are Ext⁰=Der_A(B,N). The canonical coefficient N=B⊗_A I gives precisely flat lifts, and finite presentation of B implies finite presentation of every flat lift.

Assume AC. H⁰ of the cotangent complex is the differential module; its truncation in degrees ≥−1 is the naive cotangent complex and computes Ext⁰ and Ext¹. For a smooth ring or scheme morphism L is the locally free differential module in degree zero; for an étale morphism L is zero.

Assume AC. For a smooth degree-d hypersurface in Pⁿ_k with n≥2 and d≥1, embedded deformations over local Artin k-algebras are residue-normalized degree-d equation lifts modulo units. The functor is pro-represented by the completion of P(S_d∨) at [f], is formally smooth, and has tangent space (S/(f))_d of dimension binomial(n+d,n)−1.

concerns.concern: Statement: 'If the special fibre G_k is proper and geometrically connected, then G is proper over R.' Nonemptiness is absent, although Proof 3.1 explicitly uses 'nonempty'. The opened supplier def-geometrically-reduced-integral-connected-fibre declares the empty geometric fibre connected. Take R=C[[t]], an elliptic curve E/C, and G=E×_C Spec C((t)), viewed over R. This is smooth, separated, finite type, quasi-projective and connected, with abelian generic fibre and empty proper geometrically connected special fibre, but is not proper over R. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich consumer uses the identity subgroup, whose unit guarantees nonemptiness; that use does not supply the missing hypothesis in this lemma.

Statement (b) asserts a 'smooth projective-space bundle ... on arbitrary tests' for general projective geometrically integral A, without assuming a rational point. Proof 2.1 replaces an arbitrary Picard-sheaf test class by an actual line bundle L and identifies its fibre with P((p_*L)∨); a sheaf class need not admit such a representative on that test. For a nonsplit real conic, the geometric degree-d class for odd sufficiently large d is a real point of the fppf Picard sheaf, but its effective-divisor fibre has no real point: every real effective divisor has even degree. It therefore cannot be a projective space over R. The fibre is a Brauer–Severi form. The relevant distinction and descent argument were checked in [Liedtke, Theorem 3.4 and Remark 3.5](https://math.nyu.edu/~tschinke/books/simons15/submitted/brauerseveri5.pdf), PDF pp. 13–15. Adjudication should determine whether 'projective-space bundle' was intended only fppf-locally; the stated all-test formula requires a qualification. The owned Picard-representation consumer specializes to abelian varieties with an identity point, where this obstruction vanishes.

Page line 18 identifies the conic Hilbert component as P(S_2). The opened projective-bundle definition uses the quotient convention, and the assigned example correctly identifies the coefficient-line parameter scheme as P(S_2∨). The page should preserve that dual convention; the dimension P^5 is unchanged.

Resolution-independence is applied to the standard resolution, not to an unsupported arbitrary degreewise polynomial object.
